Tanner —

Appreciate the clear asks. Draft attached: a one-page MAP with the evaluation timeline and an accompanying token-econ workbook. High-level summary here so your leadership can scan:

1) Baseline workload assumptions (please confirm):
   - Interactive chat: 25k session starts / month, average 320 tokens input + 480 tokens output per session => ~20M tokens/mo
   - Embeddings: 200k vectors / month, average 1536 tokens processed across calls => ~6M tokens/mo
   - Total baseline tokens: ~26M tokens/mo

2) Unit economics (hosted API list price parity used for modeling):
   - Model baseline: redwood-llama-16k (quantized) equivalent cost = $3.50 per 1M inference tokens (net after committed discounts modeled)
   - Estimated baseline cost: 26 * $3.50 = $91 / month (in thousands -> see workbook for full math)

3) Caching assumptions and impact:
   - Prefix caching: assume 12% of chat sessions are identical or share identical prompts => reduces input tokens by ~8% overall
   - KV cache reuse for multi-turn: assume average KV hit rate 45% for sessions with >1 turn (reduces decode tokens by up to 35% on multi-turn flows)
   - Combined effective token reduction: ~18% under baseline workload

4) Batching and throughput knobs:
   - Continuous batching target: 8-12 token-level batch size during peak; expected 12% unit-cost reduction compared to no-batching for short requests
   - We model a conservative 7% additional cost reduction from batching for Acme's mix

5) Risk scenarios / guardrails:
   - If token consumption spikes 2x, we will trigger rate-limited fallback to a smaller model variant (redwood-lite-8k) and notify your billing contact
   - Can enable per-route hard quotas and soft throttles in the MAP during evaluation

6) Evaluation plan (2-week):
   - Week 1: onboarding, synthetic load to validate latency SLOs (p95 < 350ms for chat), check cache hit telemetry and batch stats
   - Week 2: pilot with real traffic (10% of production), monitor cost, regression checks on quality, three checkpoints with Acme PM

Deliverables I attached: MAP-draft-Acme-20260610.pdf, token-econ-model-acme-20260610.xlsx, evaluation-plan-acme.docx.

Next steps: Karthik and Marissa will follow with more explicit gating numbers and a redline-ready MAP for Legal. Can we set a 30-minute sync tomorrow 10am PT to walk the model with your finance lead?

—Sean

Quick math and conservative assumptions to include in the MAP (pulling numbers from our product telemetry):

- Token pricing used in workbook: $3.50 / 1M inference tokens (applies to the quantized redwood-llama-16k path). We also model a fallback path at $1.10 / 1M for redwood-lite-8k for throttles.

- Cache hit sensitivity table (recommend including this table as a single-row summary in MAP):
   • Prefix cache hit: low 5% | base 12% | high 25%
   • KV cache reuse: low 20% | base 45% | high 65%
   • Effective token reduction: low 3% | base 18% | high 40%

- Batching assumptions:
   • Typical batch window: 8–15ms for chat bucket; modeled cost uplift 0.93x relative to single-request path when batching is enabled
   • For embeddings, we recommend micro-batching (batch size 16–32) during non-peak windows to avoid latency regressions; modeled 10–15% cost reduction in that path.

- Quality vs cost guardrail: include explicit acceptance criteria that quality delta (ROUGE-like eval or human-sampled pass rate) must be <4% degradation when moving to the quantized production profile. If not met, pause rollout and schedule a model reconfiguration.

I'll push an annotated tab in the workbook with the sensitivity ranges and a short one-paragraph explanation for Legal.
